verdicts.reason: The per-vacuum sensor loop is gated on data['maps'] membership and there is no add-path; the onboarding order guarantees the map does not exist at the only reload.
verdicts.evidence: sensor/__init__.py:97-98 `maps = manager.data.get("maps", {}); for vacuum_entity_id in maps.keys():` — every per-vacuum sensor (profile, maintenance, dock, theme, onboarding, map_overlays, battery, both error sensors) is appended inside that loop (lines 108-188). setup/workflow.add_vacuum (setup/workflow.py:99-118) only calls ensure_vacuum_record + registers a panel — it never touches data['maps']. services/setup.py:162-167 reloads the entry AFTER add_vacuum; setup_import_active_map (services/setup.py:170-178) creates the map bucket and does NOT reload — grep for 'reload' across services/setup.py and setup/workflow.py returns only that one site plus comments. The four callbacks registered at sensor/__init__.py:346-365 are all room-scoped (register_room_update_callback x2, room_history, room_rule_status); the theme callback at :377 only refreshes already-built sensors. Sibling contrast verified: button.py:32-33 iterates data['vacuums'], so reset buttons exist for a vacuum whose maintenance sensors do not. Note one imprecision in the finding that does not change the verdict: ensure_map_bucket has ~40 callers, not only the import path — but none of them reload the entry either.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced end-to-end against the real sensor and button platforms. A managed vacuum with no imported map produces ZERO sensor entities and 7 button entities. data['maps'][vac] is written only by maps/map_manager.ensure_map_bucket (the import/mapping paths); ensure_vacuum_record touches only data['vacuums']. Only two async_reload sites exist in the whole integration (services/setup.py:166 after add_vacuum, __init__.py:462 on options change) — setup_import_active_map does NOT reload, so the reload happens strictly before the map exists.

verdicts.reason: Both halves verified: the producer defaults a missing attribute to 0 while setting source_available=True, and HA genuinely drops extra_state_attributes when an entity is unavailable.
verdicts.evidence: maintenance/manager.py:709-716: `state = self._manager.hass.states.get(source_entity); if state is not None: try: current_usage = float(state.attributes.get("usage_hours", 0)); source_available = True` — an UNAVAILABLE entity still yields a non-None state object, so source_available is True and the `, 0` default wins. sensor/maintenance.py:95 `now_available = bool(result.get("source_available", True))` then feeds _attr_available, so the docstring guard at sensor/maintenance.py:28-29 never fires. Premise verified by execution against the installed HA in the docker image: Entity.__async_calculate_state contains `available = self.available ... if available: if state_attributes := self.state_attributes: attr |= state_attributes; if extra_state_attributes := self.extra_state_attributes: attr |= extra_state_attributes` — extra attributes are only merged when available, so usage_hours is absent on an unavailable source. state_class 'measurement' is set at sensor/maintenance.py:58, so the fabricated full-life value does reach long-term statistics.

verdicts.reason: Executed against the real MaintenanceManager.get_maintenance_remaining and the real EufyVacuumMaintenanceRemainingSensor, using a genuine homeassistant.core.State for the unavailable source. HA's Entity.__async_calculate_state gates `extra_state_attributes` behind `if available:` — verified in the installed HA 2026.6.0b0 source — so an unavailable source entity's State really does lack usage_hours while still being a non-None object. The `, 0` default at maintenance/manager.py:713 then wins and source_available is set True on the same line.
verdicts.evidence:
Same sensor, three source states (baseline reset_at_usage_hours=66.0, interval 150h):
  A healthy (usage_hours=108): available=True native_value=108.0 used_since_reset=42.0
  B UNAVAILABLE (attrs dropped by HA): available=True native_value=150.0 used_since_reset=0.0 current_usage=0.0 source_available=True
  C entity absent from state machine: available=False native_value=None
Class docstring (sensor/maintenance.py:28-29) claims "Returns available = False (and native_value = None) when the source entity is unavailable" — case B falsifies it. state_class='measurement' (line 58) means 150.0 is ingested into long-term statistics. Contrast confirmed at maintenance/manager.py:369 `float(replacement_state.attributes.get("usage_hours"))` with NO default, which raises→None. NOTE: the finding's prose transposes the numbers (a healthy 108h/66h baseline reads 108.0 remaining, not 42.0); the fabricated-value half — 150.0 remaining, used_since_reset 0.0, source_available true — is exact.

verdicts.reason: Per-site classification is exactly right and the destructive sites do a registry delete with a prefix that is ambiguous across sibling vacuums.
verdicts.evidence: sensor/__init__.py:255-269 and :312-325 both compute `prefix = f"{vacuum_entity_id.replace('.', '_')}_{map_id}_"`, select stale_ids by startswith + not-in-desired, then call `_registry.async_remove(entity_id)` — destructive. :285 and :341 only call _request_entity_state_write — benign, confirmed. Unique ids are built by entity_helpers.make_room_unique_id:71-72 as `f"{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}"`, so for (vacuum.alfred, map_id='2') the prefix is 'vacuum_alfred_2_', which is a genuine prefix of every unique id belonging to vacuum.alfred_2 on ANY map. Those ids are absent from desired_entities (built only from alfred's map 2 rooms), so they are swept. setup/delete.py:136-146 confirms the wider second sweep: same prefix, `entry.platform == DOMAIN and entry.unique_id.startswith(prefix)` with no dict-membership constraint, matching the sibling's theme_state, dock_events, map_overlays, maintenance and battery ids too. The async_remove-vs-re-add race in the tail is correctly self-flagged by the finder as needing runtime and I did not settle it.

verdicts.reason: The reader genuinely ignores both the map_id key and the staleness keys that the writer maintains; the writer-side guard and its comment are where the finding says they are.
verdicts.evidence: sensor/map_overlays.py:50-55 `entry = cache.get(self._vacuum_entity_id) or {}; res = entry.get("result")` — entry['map_id'] is never consulted. mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:78-135: the entry is written as `{"mtime": mtime, "map_id": str(map_id), "result": result}` and the hold path is guarded by `cached.get("map_id") == str(map_id)  # never serve another map's geometry`, and stamps `stale`, `stale_since`, `stale_reason` onto the held result. sensor/map_overlays.py:90-111 exposes present/backend/current_room/visibility/rooms/anchors and none of the three stale keys, so a held map reports present:true with no signal for up to _STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS. verdicts.reason: Branch-free source path: _result() (map_overlays.py:50-55) reads only cache[vac]['result'] and never consults cache[vac]['map_id'], while the producer maintains that key precisely as a guard — map_source_coordinator.py:117 `cached.get("map_id") == str(map_id)  # never serve another map's geometry`. Forgotten-override-sibling shape confirmed: the guard is wired into the writer only. extra_state_attributes (lines 90-111) emits present/backend/current_room/visibility/rooms/anchors and never stale, stale_since or stale_reason, which the coordinator stamps at lines 126-130; _STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS = 6*3600 confirms the 6-hour window.
verdicts.evidence: map_overlays.py:52-55 `entry = cache.get(self._vacuum_entity_id) or {}; res = entry.get("result")` — entry['map_id'] never read. The single-slot per-vacuum cache plus the sensor's per-vacuum (not per-map) identity means the reader structurally cannot detect a map mismatch. The fallback the finding names is real at sensor/__init__.py:453-456: `if not map_id: vac_maps = manager.data.get("maps", {}).get(vac, {}); map_id = next(iter(vac_maps), None)`. verdicts.reason: Executed: datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo returns a datetime.timezone instance, which by construction has a constant utcoffset for every date, so the naive-parse path stamps the import-time offset.
verdicts.evidence: timestamp_utils.py:8 `_LOCAL_TZ = datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo or UTC`, used at :65 `dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=_LOCAL_TZ if assume_local_naive else UTC)` with assume_local_naive defaulting to True at :32. Ran in the docker image: `repr(datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo)` -> `datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(0), 'UTC')`, type `<class 'datetime.timezone'>` — a FIXED-offset object, not a DST-aware ZoneInfo. (The container is UTC so the numeric DST divergence does not reproduce there, but the type is decisive: datetime.timezone.utcoffset ignores its argument.) The finder's own local run showing -7:00 for both January and July under a 'Pacific Daylight Time' label is consistent with this. BOUND HELD: I did not and cannot test whether any user's store still holds pre-migration naive timestamps, so the +/-1h consequence is bounded by that untested premise; the mechanism itself is settled.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced by execution with TZ=America/New_York. `datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo` returns a fixed-offset datetime.timezone, not a DST-aware zone, so the import-time offset is frozen and applied to every naive value regardless of the timestamp's own date. The default path is assume_local_naive=True (timestamp_utils.py:32,65).
verdicts.evidence:
Import occurred in July (EDT):
  _LOCAL_TZ repr: datetime.timezone(timedelta(days=-1, seconds=72000), 'EDT')
  utcoffset 2026-01-15: -04:00   utcoffset 2026-07-15: -04:00   (identical despite the label)
  parse_timestamp('2026-01-15 14:00:00') -> 2026-01-15 18:00:00+00:00
  TRUE America/New_York -> UTC for that instant = 19:00:00+00:00   (one hour off)
  parse_timestamp('2026-07-15 14:00:00') -> 18:00:00+00:00 = correct (matches import season)
The finding's own example is the mirror case (January import, July value); the ±1h bound is exact either way. Sub-claim confirmed: tests/unit/test_timestamp_utils.py passes assume_local_naive=False on BOTH naive-format tests (lines 96, 103), so the default path — and therefore _LOCAL_TZ — is never evaluated under test. Reachability depends on legacy naive records still existing in the user's store, which I cannot inspect.

The order divergence is real and WIDER than stated: 0 at room_entities.py:226 and number.py:170 (and also maps/map_manager.py:221/226/234, rooms/room_manager.py:136/145) vs 999 at entity_helpers.sort_room_items:102, queue_engine.py:94/126/247, run_plan.py:939 and profiles/manager.py:732/877 — so a record missing `order` reads 'cleans first' at the control the user sees and 'cleans last' at the engine that dispatches. Correctly labelled LATENT: build_managed_rooms always writes the keys.

verdicts.reason: No writer can store a library entry whose 'name' is Python None or empty, and the reachability path the finding names (import_theme) stringifies the value before storing — so the cited defect cannot be produced and the proposed fix would not address the outcome it describes.
verdicts.evidence: Every writer to theme['library'] coerces: import_theme themes/manager.py:537 `name = str(source_theme.get("name", "")).strip()` then rejects falsy at :542-543 `if not name: return {"ok": False, "reason": "missing_name"}` — a JSON null becomes the STRING 'None', never Python None, and is stored at :576-577 as final_name. save-as-new :267 `"name": str(name).strip() or "Untitled"`. overwrite :311 `"name": existing.get("name", "")` where existing comes from _get_theme_library_entries(), which normalizes via _normalize_theme_entry:140 `str(source.get("name") or "").strip() or "Untitled"`. rename_theme :350-351 `clean_name = str(name).strip() or "Untitled"`. preloaded.py:32-34 builds from hardcoded spec literals. So `entry.get("name", "none")` at sensor/theme.py:75 never sees None or ''. Separately, the suggested fix `(entry.get("name") or "none")` is inert against the one outcome that IS reachable (the stored literal string 'None' from an imported null), so the finding misidentifies both the mechanism and the fix.

verdicts.reason: The line-level defect is real and the user-visible symptom reproduces — but the finding MISLOCATES the mechanism, so its reachability paragraph needs correcting before it reaches the fix queue. Executed: import_theme with 'name': null does NOT store a null; it stores the STRING 'None', because import_theme itself does `name = str(source_theme.get("name", "")).strip()` (themes/manager.py:537) and 'None' is truthy so the `if not name` gate passes. The sensor's `str(entry.get("name", "none"))` (sensor/theme.py:75) fires on a RAW stored null, which needs a direct .storage edit or legacy data, not an import.
verdicts.evidence:
Executed against the real ThemeManager + real EufyVacuumThemeStateSensor:
  import_theme name=None -> {'ok': True, ...}; raw stored name = 'None' (string)
  sensor state after import_theme(name=null) -> 'None'
  sensor state with RAW stored name=None    -> 'None'
  import_theme name='' -> {'ok': False, 'reason': 'missing_name'}   <-- the empty-string half of the finding is UNREACHABLE via import
The sensor reads _manager.data['theme']['library'] directly (sensor/theme.py:60-62), bypassing _get_theme_library_entries()'s normalization (`str(source.get("name") or "").strip() or "Untitled"`, line 140) — that bypass is the real structural point. The proposed fix `(entry.get('name') or 'none')` is still correct.
